## Method

- Identical original W2 formula and input arrays; 36 operations.
- All contexts and arrays are allocated before timing.
- Warmup: at least 1 second and 20 calls per contender/size; includes result consumption, so this is not 1 second of pure kernel time.
- 31 measured samples; each sample averages enough separately timed batch calls to cover 65536 points. Every result is checksummed outside timing. Timer overhead is included.
- Contender order rotates per sample. Sizes run in ascending order.
- Direct C + copies: three heap-to-native input copies, one ordinary FFM downcall, status check, one native-to-heap output copy.
- Prepared C: one downcall and status check, no copies inside timing; output readback/checksum remains outside timing. This is NOT an end-to-end heap-array comparison.
- Reused buffers and checksum traversal make this a warm-cache experiment. No claim of cache-neutral pure arithmetic latency.
- Java and direct C are specialized; VM interprets the same program. Production VM, ABI and loader are unchanged.
- No epsilon admission, fast-math or forced FMA. No claim about untested CPUs, real density trees or tile VM.

## Correctness

All four batch sizes passed initial raw-bit gates before any timing. Java uses the unchanged `ThreeWayBenchmark.optimizedJavaBatch`; inputs come from its unchanged fixed-seed generator, including finite signed-zero/subnormal cases. This corpus does not establish NaN payload parity.
